task: Review the pi-chat repository from a security and safety perspective. Focus on trust boundaries, secrets, chat-originated inputs, attachments, Gondolin VM isolation assumptions, remote control commands, tmux worker orchestration, logging, persistent memory, and skills. Do not modify files. Produce evidence-backed findings with severity, affected files, rationale, and recommended fixes.

riskAreas.name: Secrets and token handling
riskAreas.description: Bot tokens, configured Gondolin HTTP secrets, encrypted runtime secret exchange, storage paths, and accidental disclosure.

riskAreas.name: Chat-originated input authorization
riskAreas.description: Allowed users/roles, bot filtering, mentions/triggers, DMs/groups, and remote control commands such as stop/status/compact/new.

riskAreas.name: Attachments and file boundaries
riskAreas.description: Downloaded or outgoing attachments crossing from chat into workspace or from VM to chat; path traversal, symlink, MIME, size, and host path containment risks.

riskAreas.name: Gondolin VM and mount isolation assumptions
riskAreas.description: Workspace/shared mounts, guest-to-host and host-to-guest path mapping, VM lifecycle, network/HTTP hook assumptions, and cross-channel isolation.

riskAreas.name: tmux worker orchestration and host command construction
riskAreas.description: Managed worker sessions, shell quoting, session names, dashboard attach commands, restart/kill behavior, and host-side command injection risk.

riskAreas.name: Persistent prompt inputs: memory and skills
riskAreas.description: Account/channel memory, auto-discovered skills, prompt injection persistence, cross-channel leakage, disabled skills, and skill path handling.

riskAreas.name: Logging, status, and telemetry disclosure
riskAreas.description: Chat logs, worker status snapshots, session metadata, errors, usage/status responses, and sensitive information exposure.

riskAreas.name: Supply chain and operational safety
riskAreas.description: Dependency/security posture, QEMU/Gondolin assumptions, automatic downloads, required intents, token handling in service clients, and failure modes.

task: Review the pi-chat repository from a functionality and product reliability perspective. Focus on setup flows, Discord/Telegram behavior, connect/disconnect/reconnect lifecycle, worker management, streaming/rendering, attachments, config persistence, stale locks/processes, error recovery, docs-code mismatches, and test gaps. Do not modify files. Produce evidence-backed findings with severity, affected files, user impact, and recommended fixes.

riskAreas.name: Setup and configuration flows
riskAreas.description: README, /chat-config flows, account/channel discovery, secret configuration, and user-facing error messages.

riskAreas.name: Discord and Telegram live behavior
riskAreas.description: Message ingestion, checkpoint/catch-up, mentions, replies, attachments, reconnects, and service API differences.

riskAreas.name: Conversation lifecycle and queueing
riskAreas.description: Connect/disconnect, armed state, pending jobs, active jobs, abort/new/compact/status, checkpoints, and queue semantics.

riskAreas.name: Gondolin VM lifecycle and file operations
riskAreas.description: VM startup/close/restart, mount operations, tool file operations, attachment staging, and session persistence.

riskAreas.name: Worker management
riskAreas.description: tmux worker spawn/list/status/open/kill, stale statuses, session reuse, restart behavior, and dashboard layout.

riskAreas.name: Streaming and rendering
riskAreas.description: Markdown rendering, chunking, preview edit/delete behavior, service limits, and formatting degradation.

riskAreas.name: Persistence and corruption recovery
riskAreas.description: Chat log JSONL, config files, locks, memory files, discovery cache, and recovery from partial/corrupt writes.

riskAreas.name: Tests and docs-code consistency
riskAreas.description: Missing tests, docs claims versus code behavior, package scripts, requirements, and operational caveats.
